clue.text: Stopper the pretender left out

indicators.note: out tells us the letter for left is dropped from the pretender

parts.note: a bluffer pretends to hold a stronger hand than they have

explanation.surface: Someone stops an impostor, who is then excluded.
explanation.definitionFit: A buffer is a device that cushions and halts a moving train, so it serves as a stopper.

clue.text: Man of religion is silent under Billy the Sailor

indicators.note: under, in a down clue, puts the silence word below the sailor

parts.note: Billy Budd is the sailor hero of Herman Melville's novella
hist is an old exclamation meaning be quiet

explanation.surface: A priest keeps quiet beneath a seaman called Billy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' puts HIST below BUDD in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of the Buddha's teaching is a man of that faith.

clue.text: Flower — if such a variety is one

indicators.note: variety means a different form, so the letters of the words are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A gardener wonders whether a certain type counts as a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' rearranges IF SUCH A; 'is one' links the flower to that.
explanation.definitionFit: The fuchsia is a shrub with drooping red and purple blooms.

clue.text: Clue, perhaps, to plan with new kind of geometry

indicators.note: perhaps hints the word clue may be in another order

parts.note: an idea is a plan

explanation.surface: A puzzle hint helps plan out a fresh type of geometry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' turns CLUE into EUCL.
explanation.definitionFit: Plane geometry built on the axioms of the ancient Greek Euclid is the classical kind.

clue.text: Cut board out for removal man

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone cuts a board down while working for a removals firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is the anagram signal: CUT and BOARD together are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An abductor carries a person away, so he is jokingly a man who does removals.

clue.text: How youngest sons got landed with Southwark language

parts.note: Southwark in London is known as the Borough, home of Borough Market
English is a language

explanation.surface: A remark on how the youngest boys came to speak South London dialect.
explanation.walkthrough: SOUTHWARK is a district of south London traditionally called the Borough.
explanation.definitionFit: Borough English was an old custom of inheritance by which land passed to the youngest son.

clue.text: Burmese Solomon?

parts.note: a wise man in Burma would be addressed with the Burmese honorific U before him and is a sage like Solomon

explanation.surface: A wise king imagined as a man from Burma.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the Burmese title of respect, as in U Thant; Solomon is the proverbial sage. Split U SAGE, the answer pictures the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer, meaning custom or habitual practice, splits into the Burmese honorific and a word for a wise man.

clue.text: Poetic shepherd gets kind of shirty with son

indicators.note: kind of hints the word shirty is to be taken in some altered form

explanation.surface: A pastoral figure turns irritable with his boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kind of' rearranges SHIRTY as THYRSI.
explanation.definitionFit: Thyrsis is a herdsman in Theocritus and Virgil, and Arnold's elegy for Clough bears the name.

clue.text: Find a seat

explanation.surface: An instruction to go and sit down.
explanation.walkthrough: To rumble someone is British slang for to find them out; a rumble seat folds out of the back of an old car.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to discover or see through a deception; the other is the fold-out dickey seat at the back of a vintage car.

clue.text: Mobile launcher for diving bells, we bear

definitions.text: Mobile launcher for diving bells, we bear

parts.words: Mobile launcher for diving bells, we bear
parts.note: a wheeled hut from which bathing belles once entered the sea, punning on diving bells

explanation.surface: A vehicle that deploys underwater chambers.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'bells' are belles: Victorian ladies were wheeled into the sea in these huts to bathe in private.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a wheeled beach hut drawn into the waves so that bathers could slip discreetly into the sea.

clue.text: Relax in this seat after playing cards

indicators.note: after puts the seat behind the cards in the answer

parts.note: a deck is a full pack of playing cards
a chair is a seat

explanation.surface: Take a seat and unwind once the card game is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the seat word behind the cards word.
explanation.definitionFit: A folding canvas seat on a beach or a ship's deck is made for lounging, so you relax in one.

clue.text: Some baby smiling — would gorgeous describe it?

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A doting parent wonders whether a grinning baby could fairly be called gorgeous.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a pun: something that is gorge-ous, full of gorges, could be described as a chasm.
explanation.definitionFit: An abysm is an old word for a bottomless pit or chasm, a deep gorge.

clue.text: Pot or dish of meat could be his

parts.note: hash is a dish of chopped cooked meat

indicators.note: could be says the letters of the next word may become another arrangement

explanation.surface: A diner wonders whose cooking pot or plate of meat this might be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges HIS into ISH. 'Pot' looks like a cooking pot but is the slang for cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: Pot is slang for cannabis, and hashish is the resin of the cannabis plant.

clue.text: We hear you arranged to listen to the instrument

indicators.note: We hear signals that the word you is to be taken by its sound alone

parts.note: you is pronounced like the letter U

indicators.note: arranged says the letters of the word listen are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A musician says you've organised a hearing of a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We hear' gives the letter U from the sound of 'you'; 'arranged' reorders the letters of 'listen' to follow it.
explanation.definitionFit: A utensil is a tool or implement, especially in the kitchen, and an instrument is a tool.

clue.text: The fish for a miserly person when cheap

explanation.surface: Someone looks for a bargain fish for a stingy buyer.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition needs the word 'cheap' in front: a cheapskate is a miser.
explanation.definitionFit: A skate is a flat ray-like fish; put after cheap it forms the word for a tightwad.

clue.text: He doesn't believe in anything revolutionary

explanation.surface: A sceptic refuses to accept any radical new idea.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a person who rejects all beliefs; the other is a member of the violent nineteenth-century Russian movement against the Tsar.

clue.text: Given the V-sign?

parts.note: V for victory, and victors were crowned with a wreath of bay leaves

explanation.surface: Someone has had a rude two-fingered gesture made at them.
explanation.walkthrough: The V-sign is not the insult but V for Victory; winners were crowned with bay.
explanation.definitionFit: To be crowned with a bay wreath was the classical honour for victory.

clue.text: Football field with metal support for the cross bars

definitions.text: metal support for the cross bars

explanation.surface: A pitch fitted with a framework holding up the goal's crossbar.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross bars are the grill bars of a cooking grid, not football goal crossbars.
explanation.definitionFit: American football is played on a pitch marked like a grill, and the word also means a metal frame of bars for cooking over a fire.

clue.text: Sinister delivery from Peking — bringing a duck perhaps?

definitions.text: Sinister delivery from Peking — bringing a duck perhaps?

parts.words: Sinister delivery from Peking — bringing a duck perhaps
parts.note: a left-arm spin ball in cricket named after China, read as though it were takeaway food from Beijing bringing Peking duck

explanation.surface: A takeaway arrives from a Chinese restaurant with a duck dish.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket this is a left-arm wrist-spinner's unorthodox ball; sinister means left-handed, and a duck is also a batsman's score of nought.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is the cricket term for a left-armer's wrist-spun ball that turns into a right-hander, a left-handed delivery.

clue.text: Usual practice at the animal home

parts.note: a habit is a usual practice

explanation.surface: Routine behaviour at the zoo.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitat is the natural environment where a creature lives.

clue.text: Teacher's conduct

explanation.surface: A remark about how a schoolteacher behaves.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', joining the two definitions. Usher was once a word for an assistant schoolmaster.
explanation.definitionFit: An under-master in old schools went by this title, and to lead guests to their seats is to escort them.

clue.text: Warm places, one of them famous for cricket

definitions.text: Warm places, one of them famous for cricket

parts.words: Warm places, one of them famous for cricket
parts.note: firesides, one of which gives its name to the Dickens story The Cricket on the ...

explanation.surface: Sunny venues, one renowned for the sport of cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket is the chirping insect from Dickens's Christmas book The Cricket on the Hearth, not the bat-and-ball game.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearths are fireside floors, warm spots in a house.

clue.text: Christmas or Easter, for example, is set down

parts.note: to land is to set down, as an aircraft does

explanation.surface: Festival dates are fixed in the calendar.
explanation.walkthrough: Christmas Island and Easter Island, not the festivals.
explanation.definitionFit: Christmas Island and Easter Island are examples of land surrounded by sea.

clue.text: Dress for wearing under a gown

definitions.text: Dress for wearing under a gown

parts.words: Dress for wearing under a gown
parts.note: describes the dark formal clothes Oxford students must wear beneath academic robes for exams

explanation.surface: A garment chosen to go beneath a robe.
explanation.walkthrough: At Oxford University this is the required dark suit and white bow tie or blouse worn with the academic gown.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Oxford term for formal academic clothing worn beneath the gown at examinations and ceremonies.

clue.text: Title for Remus (not relating to Romulus)

definitions.text: Title for Remus (not relating to Romulus)

parts.words: Title for Remus (not relating to Romulus)
parts.note: points away from the twin founder of Rome to the old storyteller of Joel Chandler Harris's tales, whose kinship title precedes his name

explanation.surface: A query about how to address the brother of Rome's founder.
explanation.walkthrough: Remus here is the narrator of the Brer Rabbit stories, not Romulus's twin; 'not relating' also jokes that the title is a relation's.
explanation.definitionFit: The Harris storyteller is known by the family title for a parent's brother.

clue.text: General drawback of islands

parts.note: Robert E Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War
read as draw back, the word draw is written backwards

explanation.surface: A commander names a disadvantage of island life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawback' looks like a disadvantage, but split as 'draw back' it gives WARD.
explanation.definitionFit: The Leeward group is a chain of Caribbean islands, so the word describes those islands.

clue.text: Huge musical production jettisoned — mad action

indicators.note: jettisoned means thrown overboard, so the performance word is dropped from the larger one

parts.note: gigantic means huge
a gig is a live music performance

explanation.surface: An enormous stage musical is scrapped in a crazy move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jettisoned' removes GIG from the start of GIGANTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: An antic is a grotesque or ludicrous caper, a piece of crazy behaviour.

clue.text: The narrow-minded about to form a separatist element

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for narrow-minded is placed around the small word

parts.note: insular means narrow-minded, inward-looking

explanation.surface: Bigots are about to set up a breakaway faction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'separatist element' sounds political, but it means something that keeps current or heat apart.
explanation.definitionFit: An insulator is a material that keeps electric current or heat apart, a component that separates.

clue.text: Horse-race switch in bad verse gets the bird

indicators.note: switch means the letters for horse are swapped for the letters for race

parts.note: doggerel is badly written comic verse
gee-gee, GG, is a childish word for a horse
the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorbike race on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A racing change written up in poor rhyme earns a jeering response.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switch' replaces GG with TT. 'gets the bird' suggests being booed off; here it simply means the answer is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The dotterel is a small plover, a wading bird.

clue.text: A strange boy, but he can be such a favourite!

parts.note: odd means strange
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A peculiar lad is surprisingly well liked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'favourite' is the betting sense, the horse expected to win.
explanation.definitionFit: In betting the strongest favourite has a price shorter than evens, so the bookmaker calls it this.
